newsitem.title: CHINA: China giant dam resettlement to cost $337mln in 97.
newsitem.headline: China giant dam resettlement to cost $337mln in 97.

text.p: China will spend 2.8 billion yuan in 1997 to relocate people who will be displaced by the giant Three Gorges dam project, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The money would mainly be used to move people from areas to be flooded when the mighty Yangtze River is diverted later this year, Xinhua said.
China had earmarked 5.8 billion yuan for the resettlement process in the last four years, the agency said.
Nearly 1.2 million people are to be moved as part of the project that will create a 600 square km (230 square mile) reservoir in central Hubei province.
Officials say the project will cost at least 90 billion yuan in 1993 terms, with 40 billion of that going to resettlement and excavation of cultural relics.
The cost is expected to reach at least 240 billion yuan by the time it is completed in 2009 if interest and inflation are taken into account, officials say.

Officials of the China Three Gorges Project Development Corp said last year they faced a funding shortage of one-sixth of the dam's multi-billion dollar price tag but have vowed to complete it even if sought-after foreign funding fails to materialise.
